# observe_user

Manages an Observe user bound to an SSO identity, so the user can be provisioned before their first login. Observe has no user delete operation: destroying this resource disables the user, and re-creating it requires `terraform import`. Requires an admin token; disabling needs `user:delete` and re-enabling needs `user:invite`.
## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "observe_user" "example" {
  email             = "jane.doe@example.com"
  label             = "Jane Doe"
  identity_provider = "SAML2"
  # Must match the NameID your IdP sends at login.
  identity = "jane.doe@example.com"
}

data "observe_rbac_group" "engineering" {
  name = "engineering"
}

resource "observe_rbac_group_member" "example" {
  group = data.observe_rbac_group.engineering.oid
  member {
    user = observe_user.example.oid
  }
}
```
<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) User email. Cannot be changed after creation; changing it forces a new user.
- `identity` (String) SSO identity the user is matched on at login. For `SAML2` this must equal the NameID the IdP sends; for `GOOGLE` it is the OAuth2 subject. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `identity_provider` (String) SSO identity provider the user logs in with. Cannot be changed after creation. Accepted values: `SAML2`, `GOOGLE`.
- `label` (String) User display name, set when the user is created. Afterwards the IdP manages it, so changes to this value are ignored.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) User comment.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether the user is disabled. Destroying the resource also disables the user.
- `expiration_time` (String) Time (RFC3339) at which the user expires.
- `role` (String) Legacy user role. Defaults to `reader` when unset. Prefer `observe_rbac_group_member` for access control.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `oid` (String) The Observe ID for user.
- `status` (String) Current user status as reported by Observe.
## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
# Import by user ID
terraform import observe_user.example 1414010

# Or by email, e.g. for a user already created by a first SSO login
terraform import observe_user.example jane.doe@example.com
```
